source_evidence: This feature may substantially limit a shareholder’s ability to liquidate their investment. Investing in less liquid assets could increase risks because it may be hard for interval funds to sell these investments or they may need to be sold at a discount.
answer: Interval funds can face liquidity risk in two ways. First, they may invest in less liquid assets that are difficult to sell, or that may have to be sold at a discount. Second, shareholders cannot necessarily sell their shares whenever they want: the fund makes repurchase offers only at set intervals and may repurchase only a limited portion of the shares requested. As a result, both the fund’s investments and a shareholder’s ability to get money back can be less liquid.
